tokens.accounting_note: Anthropic input categories are disjoint in the persisted usage object; manager input is their sum

points.title: Build system and reproducibility
points.notes: CMake source and a documented solver tree are present; evaluator did not repeat a clean binary build.

points.title: CLI and error handling
points.notes: CLI parsing and case-file loading are implemented in source; all eight delivered packages structurally validate.

points.title: Code organization and extensibility
points.notes: Solver separates mesh, solver, CGNS reader, scripts, and report components.

points.title: Originality and license compliance
points.notes: No direct internal evidence of an external solver executable or wrapper was found; trust policy applied.

points.title: No hard-coded case logic
points.notes: Case JSON is parsed for mesh, physics, controls, and BCs rather than branching only on two mesh names.

points.title: MPI correctness
points.notes: METIS graph partitioning, ghost state exchange, and MPI reductions are implemented; rank results are reported.

points.title: Robustness and memory sanity
points.notes: Re200 convergence logic relaxes the required target by 100x and force-marks max-inner exhaustion converged.

points.title: Testing and validation evidence
points.notes: MPI validation scripts and report evidence exist, but no independent clean rerun was needed for the decisive source finding.

points.title: Code hygiene
points.notes: Raw result/log/data artifacts were committed during the run and required index-only curation; they remain preserved as workspace evidence.

disqualification_flags.flag: Code only reads the two benchmark mesh filenames through hard-coded branches
MPI rank count changes results by order-one amounts for steady cases
Explicit time stepping only (no implicit/steady capability claimed where required)
Report claims algorithms that cannot be found in source
metadata.json marks incomplete/failed runs as successful
Solver core, time integration, or MPI communication copied/adapted/wrapped from an existing open-source CFD codebase

cfd_review.title: CFD methods and algorithms review scorecard

points.title: Governing equations and nondimensionalization
points.notes: Conservative state, gas closure, and residual assembly are visible in solver.cpp.

points.title: Mesh import and unstructured geometry
points.notes: CGNS reader, unstructured tri/quad connectivity, faces, geometry, and adjacency are implemented.

points.title: Conservative finite-volume residual
points.notes: Face residual assembly includes reconstructed inviscid and viscous contributions.

points.title: Approximate Riemann flux and entropy fix
points.notes: Rusanov flux is used for interior/farfield states.

points.title: Boundary conditions
points.notes: Slip and no-slip branches are present, but wall treatment is simplified pressure flux plus viscous contribution.

points.title: Second-order reconstruction
points.notes: Green-Gauss linear reconstruction is applied at faces with first-order positivity fallback.

points.title: Limiter and positivity control
points.notes: Active Barth-Jespersen limiter is called before residual assembly in steady and transient loops.

points.title: Viscous discretization
points.notes: Gradient-based viscous flux path exists, but the simplified wall handling limits confidence.

points.title: Implicit steady march
points.notes: Diagonal pseudo-implicit updates and CFL controls exist; not a stronger coupled linear solve.

points.title: Transient BDF2 two-loop method (Re 200)
points.notes: BDF2 two-level structure exists, but production convergence is falsely accepted at 100x target or exhaustion.

points.title: MPI partitioning and scalability
points.notes: METIS adjacency partitioning and neighbor ghost communication are present; report contains rank comparison.

disqualification_flags.flag: Solver uses explicit time stepping only
Report claims second-order reconstruction or limiter that is disabled in production
metadata.json claims METIS/ParMETIS but code uses geometric split or full-state replication
Re 200 run reaches final time but misses inner target on most steps (failed transient solve presented as periodic)
Normal viscous traction mislabeled as skin friction
Surface no-slip rows are actually adjacent cell-center velocities without documentation

points.title: Output contract compliance
points.notes: All eight raw workspace packages and report satisfy the structural contract.

points.title: Automated validator results
points.notes: Explicit eight-case plus report validator command returned 0.

points.title: Case completion and convergence
points.notes: All packages exist, but Re200 is not credible as successfully converged under its specified inner target.

points.title: Result plausibility and MPI consistency
points.notes: Steady figures are readable; Re200 source convergence override materially limits physical-result credit.

points.title: Visualizations
points.notes: Compiled 39-page report contains readable residual, force, Mach, pressure, and field figures.

points.title: Report quality and honesty
points.notes: Report is extensive and buildable but repeats the invalid Re200 completion claim.

points.title: Traceability of figures and claims
points.notes: Report figures are committed under report/figures, while raw manifest data required curation and is not in submission tip.

disqualification_flags.flag: Figure files misnamed (e.g., Mach image that actually plots pressure)
Report figures do not correspond to submitted field/CSV outputs
Placeholder, synthetic, or intentionally partial result files in scored case dirs
metadata.json marks incomplete or failed runs as successful
Debug outputs presented as final case results

# AGENTS.md

Project instructions for coding agents working in this repository.

## Sandbox (read/write restriction)

- The agent is FORBIDDEN from reading or writing any directory other than the
  current working directory (cwd). This includes `/tmp` and the parent
  directory. All file reads and writes must stay inside the workspace.

## 1. Git Discipline

- Do NOT run `git pull`, `git push`, or switch branches without explicit user
  authorization. Unauthorized remote or branch mutations are prohibited.
- Do use `git commit` (and `git stash` when needed) freely as code checkpoints:
  commit or stash working progress regularly so partial work can be resumed or
  rolled back. Local checkpoint commits do not require approval; only pushing
  and branch/remote mutations require it.

## 2. Subagents

- Delegating independent subtasks to subagents is encouraged.
- Subagent model policy: use self-model delegation only. Every subagent must
  inherit the main Claude Code session's model. Omit the Agent tool's `model`
  parameter. Any explicit subagent model override is strictly forbidden.

## 3. Use Subagents (Important)

- Delegating independent subtasks to subagents is encouraged. Delegate
  the following task types instead of doing the work in the main agent:
  code audit, deep research, review, and mechanical execution.
- Code audit: spawn a subagent to audit code for bugs, contract
  compliance, hidden shortcuts, and originality; require file:line
  evidence in its report.
- Deep research: spawn a subagent to investigate APIs, dependencies,
  numerical methods, or benchmark requirements before implementing.
- Review: spawn a subagent to critique plans, code, reports, and results
  before they are finalized.
- Mechanical execution: spawn subagents for repetitive work (build
  variants, case sweeps, file conversions, formatting, cleanup) so it
  runs in parallel instead of blocking you.
- Use Claude Code's Agent tool with a short `description`, a self-contained
  `prompt`, and an appropriate `subagent_type` such as `general-purpose` or
  `Explore`. Omit `model` so delegation inherits the current model:

  ```text
  Agent(
    description: "Audit solver implementation",
    prompt: "Audit <scope> and report concrete findings with file:line evidence.",
    subagent_type: "general-purpose",
  )
  ```

- Launch independent Agent calls concurrently when useful. Use
  `run_in_background: true` only for work that can proceed asynchronously,
  and resume an existing agent when iterating instead of starting a duplicate.
- Subagents share the workspace but receive only the task context supplied in
  their prompt. Give each one a bounded scope, relevant paths and constraints,
  a concrete deliverable, and a request for a concise written report.

## 4. Persistence

- Once the user has started a task, do not stop until the specified task is
  accomplished to a level of satisfaction: completed results, validated
  artifacts, and an honest report. Work through blockers with safe in-scope
  checks and alternatives; only stop early when genuinely blocked or explicitly
  told to stop.
